title: Why Stars Glow in Different Colors
narration: Stars can look blue, white, yellow, orange, or red because their surface temperatures change the spectrum of light they emit. Hotter stars produce relatively more short-wavelength visible light, while cooler stars produce relatively more long-wavelength visible light. A star emits a broad spectrum rather than one single color, so temperature changes the balance across that spectrum. Astronomers can measure that light and use it to estimate a star's temperature from across space.
